Typography

Headers, quotes, flow text, and the Material Design 3 type scale.

Type scale

New work should use the Material Design 3 type scale. Fifteen classes map onto the --md-sys-typescale-* tokens: family, size, weight, line-height, and letter-spacing. They do not set font-style — the token named -font-family-style holds “Regular” / “Medium”, which are weights, not CSS font-style keywords.

Those classes set font-family: Roboto. The framework does not ship the font files. This page loads Roboto so the samples match the spec; your app should do the same if you use the scale.

Headers

h1–h6 have default sizes and weight 400. .light is weight 300; .thin is 200.

Blockquotes

Blockquotes emphasize a quote or citation. The left bar uses --md-sys-color-primary.

This is an example quotation that uses the blockquote tag. Here is another line to make it look bigger. 
<blockquote>
  This is an example quotation that uses the blockquote tag.
</blockquote>

Flow Text

Toggle flow-text

flow-text scales font size with the viewport so line length stays readable. Resize the window and watch the sample change, or use the button to compare with unscaled body text.

To see Flow Text in action, slowly resize your browser and watch the size of this text body change. Use the button above to toggle flow-text off and on to see the difference. 

<p class="flow-text">I am Flow Text</p>

Changing the font stack

Body type uses a system stack. Roboto is a name on that list, not a file the package serves. Override $font-stack in Sass, or set font-family in your own CSS: 

html,
button, input, optgroup, select, textarea {
  font-family: GillSans, Calibri, Trebuchet, sans-serif;
}

The default stack is -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Oxygen-Sans, Ubuntu, Cantarell, "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif. Form controls inherit the same stack. Root font-size is 14px on small screens, 14.5px from the medium breakpoint, and 15px from the large breakpoint, so header rems grow slightly on wider viewports.
